prompt.context_jp: 秋の朝の光____、甘春総合病院の放射線科に静かに差し込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 秋の朝の光____、甘春総合病院の放射線科に静かに差し込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this scene-setting detail as new information.

feedback.correct_en: The opening sentence introduces the autumn light as a fresh, newly-observed element of the scene, so neutral-description が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the light as an already-known topic, which doesn't match a story opener. を would turn 光 into an object, but 差し込む here is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: そのすぐ隣の洗面台の鏡____、これから語られる小さな物語の入口となる。
prompt.prompt_jp: そのすぐ隣の洗面台の鏡____、これから語られる小さな物語の入口となる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle identifies the mirror as precisely the thing that will serve as the entrance?

feedback.correct_en: が here highlights the mirror as the specific/identifying subject — 'it is this mirror that becomes the entrance.' This exhaustive-identification reading fits the narrator's framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just make 鏡 a bland topic and lose the 'this is the one' nuance. に would mark a location/goal, not the subject.

contrast_examples.en: It is this mirror that is the entrance.

prompt.context_jp: 鏡____映し出す
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏡____映し出す
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator frames 'the mirror' as the general topic of this short refrain.

feedback.correct_en: The refrain '鏡は映し出す' treats the mirror as the general topic — 'as for mirrors, they reflect.' This generic statement calls for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like 'it is the mirror (not something else) that reflects,' which isn't what this poetic refrain is doing. を would make 鏡 the object.

prompt.context_jp: 洗面台の前に立った広瀬____、何気なく前髪をかき上げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 洗面台の前に立った広瀬____、何気なく前髪をかき上げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose has been introduced; the sentence now describes what she does.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose is a known character the narrative is tracking; marking her as topic with は is natural when describing her next action.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal her as newly-identified, as if answering 'who brushed their bangs?' That's not the discourse here.

prompt.context_jp: 実は この病院に 1人 会いたい人____いんだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 実は この病院に 1人 会いたい人____いんだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Kumada introduces that such a person exists.

feedback.correct_en: Existential sentences with いる introducing a new entity ('there's a person I want to meet') use が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that specific person is already known — but Kumada is revealing them for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There's someone I want to meet.

prompt.context_jp: 鏡の中の自分だけ____唯一の相談相手だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏡の中の自分だけ____唯一の相談相手だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with だけ to identify the one and only confidant?

feedback.correct_en: 'Xだけが Y' is the standard exhaustive pattern — 'only X (and nothing else) was Y.' が picks out the unique subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would suggest 'at least this one, as for it…' — a contrast reading that doesn't match the uniqueness being asserted here.

prompt.context_jp: 丈夫な髪の毛____たくさん生えてくる オススメのシャンプーって 知ってたりします？
prompt.prompt_jp: 丈夫な髪の毛____たくさん生えてくる オススメのシャンプー
prompt.prompt_en: In this relative clause describing the shampoo, which particle marks 髪の毛?

feedback.correct_en: In subordinate/relative clauses describing a property ('shampoo that makes hair grow'), the embedded subject typically takes が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a relative clause would be marked and often ungrammatical here — topics generally don't live inside embedded descriptive clauses.

contrast_examples.jp: 髪が生えるシャンプー。

contrast_examples.en: As for hair, longer is better (main-clause topic).

prompt.context_jp: 父____、何か 10円ハゲが できちゃったみたいで
prompt.prompt_jp: 父____、何か 10円ハゲが できちゃったみたいで
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose is pretending it's her father who has the bald spot, introducing him here.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose brings the father into the conversation as new information — 'my father (it turns out) got a bald spot.' Neutral-description が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the father as an established topic, but she's mentioning him for the first time as a cover story.

prompt.context_jp: 整形外科の先生____呼んでます
prompt.prompt_jp: 整形外科の先生____呼んでます
prompt.prompt_en: A colleague reports who is calling Hirose.

feedback.correct_en: This is a report of a new event — someone (newly identified) is calling. Event-reporting が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the orthopedist is already the topic of discussion, which isn't the case in this sudden announcement.

contrast_examples.en: The doctor (topic) is in a meeting.

prompt.context_jp: 学校で 具合悪くなった生徒____いてさ
prompt.prompt_jp: 学校で 具合悪くなった生徒____いてさ
prompt.prompt_en: Kumada is explaining the situation for the first time.

feedback.correct_en: Existential いる introducing a brand-new referent ('there was a student who got sick') takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the student as already known, but she's being introduced to Hirose here.

contrast_examples.en: There was a kid who was sick.

prompt.context_jp: 話す人____キラキラ輝いてるかどうかで 全てが決まりますからね
prompt.prompt_jp: 話す人____キラキラ輝いてるかどうかで 全てが決まりますからね
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the speaker as the specific thing that determines everything?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded clause 'whether the speaker shines,' が marks the subject of 輝いてる. It's a subordinate-clause subject, not a main topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this embedded whether-clause would be awkward; main-clause topic marking doesn't fit here.

contrast_examples.jp: 人が輝いてるかどうか。

prompt.context_jp: そんな… 私 全然 輝いて____ません もう何 話したらいいのか…
prompt.prompt_jp: 私 全然 輝いて____ません
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose contrasts herself with the glowing image Tanaka just described.

feedback.correct_en: Negation with 全然 commonly pairs with は for emphatic contrast — '輝いてはいません' means 'shining? Not at all,' pushing back on Tanaka's claim.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would be ungrammatical with 輝いて (te-form + ません). は softens/contrasts the negated predicate; が doesn't attach this way.

prompt.context_jp: 貧血の疑いを告げる指標____控えめだったが、それだけでは説明のつかない何かが、そこに漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貧血の疑いを告げる指標____控えめだったが
prompt.prompt_en: The sentence sets up a contrast: the anemia indicators were mild, BUT something else lingered.

feedback.correct_en: The が-clause that follows signals contrast ('…were mild, but…'). は on 指標 sets up that contrast explicitly — 'as for the anemia indicators, they were mild (unlike the other thing).'
feedback.incorrect_en: Subject-が here would lose the contrastive setup that the sentence clearly demands.

contrast_examples.jp: 値は低いが、症状は重い。
contrast_examples.en: The values are low, but the symptoms are severe (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 花倉さん____骨粗しょう症です
prompt.prompt_jp: 花倉さん____骨粗しょう症です
prompt.prompt_en: Amakasu delivers the diagnosis about Hanakura.

feedback.correct_en: X は Y です is the standard 'A is B' framing when X is the established topic — here, the patient they're discussing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 花倉さんが骨粗しょう症です would answer 'who has osteoporosis?' — not the discourse here, where the patient is known and the diagnosis is new.

prompt.context_jp: 花倉さんの今の症状の原因____栄養不足です
prompt.prompt_jp: 花倉さんの今の症状の原因____栄養不足です
prompt.prompt_en: Amakasu explains what the cause is.

feedback.correct_en: The cause is the topic being explained; 'as for the cause, it's malnutrition' — standard 'X は Y です' definition pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it 'it's the cause (not something else) that is malnutrition,' which doesn't match the explanatory flow.

contrast_examples.jp: 原因がストレスだと分かった。
contrast_examples.en: It was discovered that the cause is stress.

prompt.context_jp: 細くてキレイな先生____分かりませんよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 細くてキレイな先生____分かりませんよ
prompt.prompt_en: Noa contrasts the doctor with herself — 'YOU, slim and pretty, wouldn't understand.'

feedback.correct_en: 分かる takes にはfor the experiencer when contrast is intended: 'as for YOU (unlike me), you wouldn't get it.' The は on に adds the contrastive edge.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the doctor the subject of 分からない in a neutral way, losing the pointed contrast Noa is making.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたには分からない。

prompt.context_jp: 選ばれるの____たった5人だけで
prompt.prompt_jp: 選ばれるの____たった5人だけで
prompt.prompt_en: Noa emphasizes how few get chosen.

feedback.correct_en: '選ばれるのは〜だけ' is a cleft-like structure: 'as for who gets chosen, it's only five.' は sets up this defining frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly collide with だけ here; the clefted 'as for X, …' reading needs は.

contrast_examples.jp: 合格するのは3人だけだ。

prompt.context_jp: 妹____色白で細くて 手足が長くて
prompt.prompt_jp: 妹____色白で細くて 手足が長くて
prompt.prompt_en: Noa shifts topic to describe her sister's features.

feedback.correct_en: Noa switches to the sister as new topic ('as for my sister, she's fair and slim…') — classic topic-shifting は, especially with the implicit contrast to herself.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a single reported event, losing the sustained description of the sister's traits.

prompt.context_jp: 私____仕事でミスはするし 技師としては中途半端で
prompt.prompt_jp: 私____仕事でミスはするし
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose sets herself up as the topic to self-criticize.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose makes herself the topic to describe her shortcomings — 'as for me, I make mistakes…' Natural topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would be an identifying 'it's me (who makes mistakes)' answer, which doesn't fit her general self-assessment.

prompt.context_jp: ふとした偶然が思わぬ再会を用意していることは、この病院に限らず____である。
prompt.prompt_jp: この病院に限らず____である
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the set phrase meaning 'not entirely absent / does happen.'

choices.text: ないにこしたことはない

feedback.correct_en: なきにしもあらず is a classical set phrase meaning 'it's not that there isn't any' — a literary 'it does happen.' Fits the narrator's reflective tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options exist but mean different things: 'as good as nonexistent' and 'better not to have,' neither of which matches.

contrast_examples.jp: 可能性はなきにしもあらず。
ないにこしたことはない。

prompt.context_jp: 父が 10円ハゲが できちゃったみたいで。それは ____ ですね
prompt.prompt_jp: それは ____ ですね
prompt.prompt_en: Inou's calm diagnosis of the likely cause of sudden bald spots.

feedback.correct_en: 円形脱毛症(10円ハゲ) is popularly attributed to stress, and Inou's deadpan diagnosis that follows is exactly that.
feedback.incorrect_en: Allergy or genetics aren't the standard quick explanation for 10円ハゲ in casual Japanese conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: それはストレスですね。

prompt.context_jp: 失礼ですが ____ 可能性ってありますか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 失礼ですが ____ 可能性ってありますか？
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi asks the patient a routine pre-imaging safety question.

feedback.correct_en: Before MRI/radiology on a female patient, pregnancy is the standard check — Igarashi's blunt question is exactly this.
feedback.incorrect_en: Fractures or a cold aren't the pre-imaging safety concerns being asked about here, and Noa's shocked reaction confirms 妊娠.

prompt.context_jp: 恋に仕事に____だなぁ
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋に仕事に____だなぁ
prompt.prompt_en: A teasing comment about Hirose's losing streak in both love and work.

feedback.correct_en: 〜っぱなし means 'leaving in a state of X.' 負けっぱなし = 'losing continually.' Fits the ribbing tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 勝ちっぱなし (winning streak) would reverse the meaning. 置きっぱなし refers to leaving things around, not personal fortune.

prompt.context_jp: 人って すぐに ____ じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_jp: 人って すぐに ____ じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose explains why she couldn't tell Noa to stop dieting.

feedback.correct_en: The whole scene is about people comparing themselves and others — Noa vs. her sister, Hirose vs. others. 比べる is the key verb.
feedback.incorrect_en: 諦める (give up) or 忘れる (forget) don't match the discussion about inferiority complexes from comparison.

contrast_examples.en: I end up comparing myself to others.

prompt.context_jp: 負けてる方は どんどん自分に自信をなくして ____ 抱いて
prompt.prompt_jp: ____ 抱いて
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun collocates with 抱く to describe what the 'losing' side feels?

feedback.correct_en: 劣等感を抱く ('harbor feelings of inferiority') is the fixed collocation and matches Hirose's point about losing confidence.
feedback.incorrect_en: 優越感 (superiority) and 満足感 (satisfaction) are the opposite of what the 'losing' side feels.

prompt.context_jp: 言葉で____だけじゃ 骨粗しょう症の怖さは 伝わらないと思うので
prompt.prompt_jp: 言葉で____だけじゃ
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best fits 'just conveying in words'?

feedback.correct_en: 伝える pairs with 伝わる in the next clause — 'just conveying in words won't convey the fear.' The repetition is intentional.
feedback.incorrect_en: 教える (teach) or 話す (talk) don't form the same tight pairing with 伝わらない that highlights the gap between telling and reaching.

prompt.context_jp: (広瀬が入ってくる)「____」
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase is used when someone shows up right as they are being talked about?

feedback.correct_en: 噂をすれば (short for 噂をすれば影がさす) = 'speak of the devil.' They were just discussing Hirose, and she walks in.
feedback.incorrect_en: 渡りに船 means 'just what I needed' and 猫に小判 means 'pearls before swine' — neither fits the timing joke here.

prompt.context_jp: Amakasu is gently reassuring Noa after the diagnosis.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural coming from a doctor speaking kindly to a teenage patient?

choices.text: そのままで十分キレイですよ。とにかく、食事はきちんと取ってください。
お前そのままで十分キレイだぞ。飯ちゃんと食えよ。
あなた様はそのままで十二分にお美しくございます。お食事を頂戴くださいませ。

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses です/ます with a gentle imperative (〜てください) — the right register for a doctor-patient conversation with warmth.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is far too rough/male-casual for this setting. C is exaggeratedly deferential keigo that would sound bizarre coming from a doctor to a patient.

contrast_examples.jp: 食事はきちんと取ってください。

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi makes a professional suggestion to Dr. Amakasu during a reading session.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a colleague suggesting an additional exam to a doctor?

choices.text: 先生、DEXAを検討してみたらどうですか？
先生がDEXAを検討しなさい。

feedback.correct_en: 〜てみたらどうですか is a soft, collegial suggestion — appropriate for a technician proposing to a doctor.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is blunt command form, rude between colleagues. C uses 〜なさい, which is a top-down instruction a subordinate wouldn't give to a senior.

contrast_examples.jp: 検討してみたらどうですか。

prompt.context_jp: Hirose quietly challenges the room during the conference.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best captures Hirose's hesitant-but-firm challenge?

choices.text: ホントにそう思ってますか？口ではみんな、見た目は二の次とか言いながら、結局みんなキレイな人が好きじゃないですか。
ホントにそう思ってますか？口ではみんな、見た目が二の次とか言いながら、結局みんなキレイな人は好きじゃないですか。
本当にそう思うか？結局みんな綺麗な奴が好きだろ。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the source: 見た目は二の次 (contrastive は — 'looks, at least, are secondary') and キレイな人が好き (identifying が — it's pretty people that people like). The particles track discourse roles correctly.
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps the particles: 見た目が二の次 loses the contrastive framing, and キレイな人は好きじゃない flips the meaning to 'don't like pretty people.' C is too blunt/male for Hirose.

prompt.context_jp: The chief engineer returns from vacation and hands out souvenirs to the team.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a friendly 'help yourself' to coworkers?

choices.text: 土産だ みんな食え
お土産でございます。皆様、お召し上がりくださいませ。
土産を購入しました。各自摂取してください。

feedback.correct_en: The source line is blunt and warm — typical of the chief's gruff-but-friendly register with his team.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is customer-service keigo, wildly out of place among coworkers. C sounds like a sterile announcement, not a casual offer of snacks.

contrast_examples.jp: お召し上がりください。

prompt.context_jp: Inou hands the booklet to Hirose and asks her to pass it on.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing captures Inou's gentle-but-firm 'please do this for me' tone?

choices.text: まあ そう言わずに 渡してみてください 頼みましたよ
まあ そう言わないで 渡すこと 命じます
そんなこと言うな 絶対渡せ

feedback.correct_en: そう言わずに softens the request, 〜てみてください invites her to try, and 頼みましたよ lands it with warm insistence — exactly Inou's calm style.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is unnaturally formal/command-like (命じます). C is aggressive imperative, out of character for Inou's tone with Hirose.

contrast_examples.jp: そう言わずに頼みますよ。
contrast_examples.en: Don't say that — I'm counting on you.
